assertion.statement: The finite binary construction uses one actual finite anticyclotomic character Psi_i for every constituent, prescribing exponent1 at every oriented prime of the full graph Q, including unused primes and augmentation.
assertion.objects: Ai=(Z/2^i)[t]/t^i, Ai[G], the fixed Tate lattice T2E, universal quadratic character and actual Psi_i=(1+t)^xi_i.
assertion.hypotheses: The fixed curve, parametrization and local types, finite graph Q, and the moving-character realization theorem with its permitted prescriptions are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: For every fixed finite binary family and every finite precision i, before evaluating any character.
assertion.parameter_range: Imaginary K split at2N, excluding Q(i) and Q(sqrt(-3)); active primes good split, derivative primes good inert outside current support.
assertion.uniformity: The trace bound depends on fixed E, not the number of graph primes; Q is fixed before selecting the sequence of moving primes.
assertion.constants: Exponent1 is prescribed at every oriented graph prime; the moving prime varies with precision.
assertion.normalizations: Use actual derived Kummer, unramified, full and orthogonal local maps and homotopies, and retain the integral determinant basis. The varying quadratic character is trivial at real and2N places.
assertion.exceptional_cases: No single fixed odd prime is claimed to support an infinitely ramified Z2 character. Unused graph primes and augmentation are not omitted.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the entire finite family and Q; construct the actual finite character at each precision; retain local maps and determinant basis; only then evaluate constituents and pass to the indicated limits.

assertion.statement: For the actual complex conjugation tau, the finite twisted module has an Ri-linear perfect identification tau*Mi=Mi*(1), fixing t and the group basis; with conjugate places and actual orthogonal local maps this yields coefficient-valued shifted Selmer duality.
assertion.objects: The actual tau with tau²=1, finite anticyclotomic ring-class character, universal rational quadratic character, Tate module and transported Weil pairing e2(v,rho(tau)w).
assertion.hypotheses: The finite character family, perfect equivariant Weil pairing, ring-class conjugation inversion and Selmer duality with the actual local orthogonality and isotropy homotopies are supplied.
assertion.quantifiers: Each finite precision and scalar or binary coefficient ring Ri=Ai orAi[G].
assertion.parameter_range: The fixed imaginary quadratic K and actual finite coefficient modules, before limits.
assertion.uniformity: The same coefficient convention and maps persist through both retained limits; no averaging or group-order denominator is introduced.
assertion.constants: The duality shift is -3; tau²=1 and the quadratic character equals its inverse.
assertion.normalizations: Pull back the Galois action without acting on Ri. The inverse of1+t is accounted for by the pulled-back character. At derivative primes the pairing includes J.
assertion.exceptional_cases: A nonquadratic twist is not identified with its ordinary dual. Full local complexes become zero only where their actual contractions exist.
assertion.limit_order: Use ring-class inversion to identify the conjugate character; construct the coefficient pairing; transport local places and orthogonal maps with homotopies; apply finite Selmer duality and retain those maps.
